newsitem.title: UK: London gold fixes barely changed, takes stock.
newsitem.headline: London gold fixes barely changed, takes stock.

text.p: An early short covering rally in gold soon peaked on Tuesday and the bullion market turned flat ahead of economic testimony before Congress on Wednesday by U.S. Federal Reserve chairman Alan Greenspan.
Gold fixed at $353.10 per ounce, just 35 cents off the morning setting and five cents above the fixing on Monday afternoon.
The Comex April futures contract was up $0.10 at $355.30 shortly after the 1500 GMT fixing.
"It is slightly overbought, and I emphasise slightly, so we may see some consolidation before a challenge of $360.30," said technical analyst Karen Jones at Credit Suisse First Boston.
Dealers said spot bullion prices were caught in a narrow range of between $350.00-$355.00 at the outside following a recovery from 3-3/4 year lows of around $336.00 on February 12.

Selling from Australian producers in the Far East edged prices lower during Asian trading but there were sufficient net gains left in the price to spark short covering when Europe opened after having placed sell orders overnight.
"It is waiting for a breakout and there might be slight bias towards the upside," one dealer said.
However dealers emphasised that recent statements from Fed chairman Greenspan had sent a frisson through the paper investment markets.
The precious metals would be treading carefully ahead of his semi-annual Humphrey-Hawkins testimony before the Senate Banking Committee at 1500 GMT on Wednesday.
The market took some heart from a statement from the head of the Belgian central bank, Alfons Verplaetse that the bank had an appropriate balance of gold in its reserves following recent sales.
Palladium continued to firm fixing at $140.00, a dollar ahead of Monday, as the trade and speculators bought metal against the delayed start to Russia-Japan exports.

Backgrounding the delayed start to shipments - assumed to be beginning in April at the earliest - was possible labour problems at the Norilsk production facility were workers salaries have gone unpaid.
Platinum was unchanged from Monday's close at $373.00/$374.00 and silver was three cents lower at $5.18/$5.21 and attracting the least attention of the complex's market.
